raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_GLM_NEXTN_MOE_PTPC=1`, GLM NextN adds a per-channel FP8 scheme for routed experts, but also maps checkpoint per-expert excludes into runtime names. Quark treats those leaf exclusions as excluding the fused expert module, so its quantization method is never selected even though the loader converts the expert weights to FP8.

## Modifications

Skip mapped routed-expert leaf exclusions when the existing PTPC predicate is enabled. Preserve checkpoint exclusions for loading, other runtime exclusions, flag-off behavior, and the shared-expert fusion guard. Add a regression using Quark's actual ignore predicate.

## Accuracy Tests

Using the same test file on base and patched trees:

- Existing registered PTPC suite: base reproduces the new assertion; patched passes all 12 tests without skips.
- CPU component check with real QuarkConfig and FusedMoE types: base selects no quant method with PTPC enabled; patched selects QuarkFusedMoEMethod and the per-channel FP8 scheme. The real parameter loader correctly places both experts' gate/up/down weights and scales. Flag-off and shared-expert BF16 behavior are preserved.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured; this fixes quantization configuration selection and makes no performance claim.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

_Disclosure: Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom) session analysis, reviewed and validated by human._

files.patch:
@@ -1393,16 +1393,22 @@ def _resolve_nextn_quant_config(self, config, quant_config):
         if not mtp_excluded:
             return quant_config
 
+        apply_ptpc = should_apply_glm_nextn_moe_ptpc(
+            quant_config, config.num_hidden_layers
+        )
+        routed_experts_prefix = "model.decoder.mlp.experts."
         names = set(quant_config.exclude_layers)
         for name in mtp_excluded:
-            names.add(self._map_mtp_ckpt_name(name, layer_prefix))
-
-        # Fused routed experts are queried by the coarse module prefix
-        # "model.decoder.mlp.experts", which expanded per-expert leaf excludes
-        # do not match. So that module needs its own entry: bf16 as in the
-        # checkpoint, or the scheme matching the on-load PTPC-FP8 cast.
-        # Same gate as the weight-loader cast (Quark-excluded = bf16 in ckpt).
-        if should_apply_glm_nextn_moe_ptpc(quant_config, config.num_hidden_layers):
+            mapped = self._map_mtp_ckpt_name(name, layer_prefix)
+            # Keep checkpoint excludes for the loader, but let the converted
+            # runtime experts use the PTPC scheme below.
+            if apply_ptpc and mapped.startswith(routed_experts_prefix):
+                continue
+            names.add(mapped)
+
+        # Match the runtime scheme to the weight-loader cast; otherwise keep
+        # the checkpoint's BF16 routed experts excluded.
+        if apply_ptpc:
             mtp_layer_quant_config = quant_config.quant_config.setdefault(
                 "layer_quant_config", {}
             )

         self.assertEqual(scheme["input_tensors"]["qscheme"], "per_channel")
